name: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig
product_name: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig
description:
The SlipThread MX-3 is a personal urban cable-transit harness system manufactured by Ringo Corponation, designed for individual rapid traversal of GLMZ's vertical built environment. Unlike the DriftPack RV-6 vectored thrust harness, the MX-3 operates on pre-tensioned synthetic fiber cables — called 'threads' — anchored between buildings at heights between 20 and 200 meters. The user wears a low-profile chest and shoulder rig housing a motorized grip-and-release carriage mechanism, braking regenerative coils, and a Cinderblock AI micro-routing chip that calculates descent angles, load tolerances, and junction transfer points in real time. Threads themselves are maintained under licensed networks in Tier 1 and 2 districts, with Ringo charging monthly access fees for use of certified anchor points. The carriage mechanism reaches travel speeds of up to 60 km/h on a favorable grade and can execute mid-line transfers at junction nodes — small anchor platforms bolted to building facades where multiple cable routes intersect.

The MX-3 was originally marketed to corporate courier services and building maintenance contractors as a faster alternative to elevator banks in dense arcology clusters. Its adoption as a personal mobility system by Tier 1 and 2 residents followed after Tessera Corponation integrated SlipThread access nodes into several of its high-rise residential towers as a premium amenity. The system's social stratification is immediate and visible: certified Ringo network threads are color-coded with luminescent jacketing in upper-tier districts, while the outer rings run unlicensed black-market threads of wildly variable quality — salvaged synthetic cable, improvised anchor bolts, and carriage mechanisms cannibalizedprimarily from the MX-3's own gray-market component supply chain.

social_impact: The SlipThread MX-3 has created a visible class division written directly into the skyline: in wealthy districts, the luminescent certified thread network is a deliberate architectural feature, a display of connectivity and premium citizenship. In outer-ring zones, the black-market thread networks are dense, tangled, and regularly lethal — anchor failures, overloaded cables, and untested carriage mechanisms produce a steady casualty rate that Ringo's legal team has spent considerable resources ensuring cannot be traced back to component liability. The ability to move rapidly through vertical space without touching the street has become a marker of status and safety simultaneously, since street-level in many districts is genuinely dangerous.
story_hooks: Someone is systematically cutting certified Ringo threads in a Tier 2 district — not the anchors, just the cables, precisely, in sequence, as if following a map
A Cinderblock AI routing chip in an MX-3 rig begins directing its user to junction nodes that aren't on any official network map — and the threads there are definitely not Ringo-manufactured
A corporate executive is found dead at a thread junction platform in a district she had no business being in — her certified rig shows she traversed six unlicensed threads to get there

Ringo is rolling out MX-4 with a mandatory biometric lock — the entire black-market MX-3 ecosystem is about to be rendered incompatible, and the outer-ring communities that depend on it are organizing
